title: Log Management and Monitoring
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 6: Security Assessment and Testing: Log Management and Monitoring.

items: Collect logs from all security-relevant systems (firewalls, IDS, servers, applications)
Logs must be protected from tampering (write-once storage, digital signatures)
Centralized log management — Aggregate logs in a single location
Log retention — Keep logs long enough for compliance and forensics
Time synchronization (NTP) — Essential for correlating events across systems
Security Information and Event Management — Centralizes log analysis
Real-time correlation of events from multiple sources
Alerting on suspicious patterns and policy violations
Compliance reporting — Automated reports for auditors
Examples: Splunk, IBM QRadar, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic SIEM
Log aggregation — Collect logs from diverse sources
Normalization — Convert different log formats to common format
Correlation — Identify relationships between events
Alerting — Notify on matching rule or anomaly
Dashboards — Visual representation of security posture
Forensic analysis — Search and investigate historical events

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: SIEM is for MONITORING and ANALYSIS. It requires proper configuration of rules and baselines to be effective. A SIEM without tuning produces too many false positives and becomes "shelfware."

items: Ongoing assessment of security controls and risk posture
Automates detection of configuration drift and new vulnerabilities
Supports near real-time awareness of security state
Required by NIST SP 800-137 and FISMA
Includes: vulnerability scanning, configuration management, log monitoring
